words.sense: Philosophical rejection of inherent meaning or value
misconceptions: Confusing it with mere depression or negative mood.

words.sense: Distrust of human motives or sincerity
misconceptions: Assuming it implies believing existence is totally void of point.

semantic_axes.description: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
Whether the attitude involves active, distrustful engagement with others (cynicism) or passive, resigned detachment from all value (nihilism).

nihilism: He rejected the idea that any action matters, viewing all human endeavors as a descent into nihilism.
The philosophical school of nihilism argues that existence is inherently void.
She found a strange comfort in nihilism, knowing that nothing mattered in the grand cosmic scale.
His nihilism led him to abandon all moral constraints.
Nihilism can be a dangerous, passive embrace of the void.
The text suggests that nihilism is the inevitable end of rational thought.
cynicism: His cynicism grew every time he saw a politician promise change while taking bribes.
Despite her idealism, she developed a sharp cynicism about human nature.
The manager's cynicism meant he never believed a word his employees said.
Such deep cynicism prevented her from trusting any charity.
His cynicism was a defense mechanism against being hurt by others again.
Political cynicism is widespread in modern society.

nihilism: She didn't believe her boss was cheating; her nihilism didn't extend to office politics.
He was a nihilist because he hated his neighbor (Wrong: that's social distrust/cynicism).
It was total nihilism when he decided not to eat that cake (Wrong: triviality).
The student believed people were selfish, thus proving nihilism (Wrong: that's cynicism).
Her nihilism was shattered when she fell in love (Wrong: love doesn't disprove nihilism).
He thought the film was bad, proving his nihilism (Wrong: subjective taste).
cynicism: He believed the universe was a cold, meaningless accident: true cynicism (Wrong: nihilism).
She practiced cynicism by refusing to acknowledge any objective truth (Wrong: nihilism).
His cynicism meant he thought atoms don't exist (Wrong: not cynicism).
Cynicism is the belief that physics is fake (Wrong: unrelated).
She felt that life was empty, so she was in a state of cynicism (Wrong: nihilism).
He distrusted the laws of gravity, showing his cynicism (Wrong: absurdity).

edges.boundary_rule: If the problem is 'human selfishness', use cynicism; if the problem is 'the universe is inherently pointlessly void', use nihilism.

misconceptions.M1: I am depressed/sad, so I am a nihilist.
misconceptions.M2: I distrust people, so life must have no meaning.
misconceptions.M3: I don't think there is a god, so I must believe in nothing (nihilism).

beats.text: Marcus sees his government officials passing bills that only benefit their donors.
He thinks they've done this for decades, assuming no one in power is actually honest.

chains.feedback_short: Marcus focuses on the selfish motives of people, not the nature of existence.
chains.feedback_deep: Marcus distrusts the people in power, believing they are selfish. This is a classic example of cynicism, which targets human motives, rather than nihilism, which denies all meaning.
chains.contrast_rule: If it's about selfish people, it's cynicism; if it's about the void, it's nihilism.

hints.attention: Does he doubt the existence of truth, or just the honesty of these specific people?
hints.axis: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
hints.contrast: If it's about selfish people, it's cynicism; if it's about the void, it's nihilism.

beats.text: Elena looks at the painting of a vast, empty landscape and feels that it captures the pointlessness of our existence.
She tells her friends that this image represents the absolute lack of inherent purpose in the universe.

chains.feedback_short: Elena describes the lack of cosmic purpose, which defines nihilism.
chains.feedback_deep: Elena's interpretation focuses on the lack of purpose in the universe, which is the core of nihilism. She isn't criticizing people's motives.
chains.contrast_rule: Focus on motive = cynicism; focus on cosmic emptiness = nihilism.

hints.attention: Is she criticizing the artist's motives, or the nature of existence itself?
hints.axis: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
hints.contrast: Focus on motive = cynicism; focus on cosmic emptiness = nihilism.

beats.text: David watches his date smile, but he instantly assumes she is only interested in his bank account.
beats.decisive_clue: assumes she is interested in money

beats.text: He thinks that everyone is ultimately acting out of pure, calculated self-interest, regardless of what they say.

chains.feedback_short: David's focus on the selfish motives of his date defines cynicism.
chains.feedback_deep: David is judging his date's motives, believing them to be purely selfish. This is cynicism, not nihilism, which is about the lack of objective meaning in the universe.
chains.contrast_rule: Distrusting individuals = cynicism; denying all purpose = nihilism.

hints.attention: Does he doubt his date's intentions, or does he doubt that anything matters?
hints.axis: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
hints.contrast: Distrusting individuals = cynicism; denying all purpose = nihilism.

beats.text: Ken sees the entire concept of charity as a futile exercise because he believes there is no objective good or bad in this universe.
He then watches a celebrity donate money and claims they are only doing it to boost their own image for profit.

chains.feedback_short: Ken flips from denying objective moral value (nihilism) to suspecting selfish motives (cynicism).
chains.feedback_deep: Initially, Ken questions the very existence of moral value, which is nihilism. When he targets the celebrity's selfish intent, he pivots to cynicism, which is about doubting individual motives.
chains.contrast_rule: If it's about the universe's lack of value, it's nihilism; if it's about a person's greed, it's cynicism.

hints.attention: Does he still focus on the cosmic void, or is he now accusing someone of a hidden agenda?
hints.axis: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
hints.contrast: If it's about the universe's lack of value, it's nihilism; if it's about a person's greed, it's cynicism.

beats.text: Sarah reads the headlines and assumes every single story is skewed to push a corporate agenda.
She further claims that, ultimately, nothing reported in any outlet holds true weight, as truth itself is merely a convenient fiction in a purposeless world.

chains.feedback_short: Sarah flips from distrusting reporters' motives (cynicism) to denying truth itself (nihilism).
chains.feedback_deep: Sarah starts with cynicism, doubting the reporters' motives. She then expands her view to a nihilistic claim that truth itself has no objective reality or meaning in our world.
chains.contrast_rule: Distrusting individuals = cynicism; denying all absolute truth = nihilism.

hints.attention: Is she criticizing the reporters, or attacking the very concept of objective reality?
hints.axis: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
hints.contrast: Distrusting individuals = cynicism; denying all absolute truth = nihilism.

chains.frame: How Maya views the hotel review: ___

beats.text: Maya thinks the five-star review was written by an employee, not a real guest.
She assumes all such reviews are just manufactured attempts to trick tourists, proving that no one can be trusted.

chains.feedback_short: Maya distrusts the reviewer, and her attitude remains cynical.
chains.feedback_deep: Maya continues to be skeptical of human behavior, now applying it to all hotel reviews. She is still being cynical (distrusting motives), even though she is expressing a broader sentiment.
chains.contrast_rule: Suspect selfish motives = cynicism; deny existence's meaning = nihilism.

hints.attention: Is she talking about the void of the universe, or the dishonest people?
hints.axis: Whether the focus is on the cosmic/existential void (nihilism) or interpersonal/human motives (cynicism).
hints.contrast: Suspect selfish motives = cynicism; deny existence's meaning = nihilism.
